caption: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, Disjunctive Reasoning, and Conjunctive Reasoning.
model_annotation: The figure contains three grayscale pie charts showing the distribution of quantifier and operation types across tasks titled “Categorical,” “Approximate Number Generation,” and “Disjunctive & Conjunctive.” The Categorical chart has four slices with percentage labels inside the wedges: “Universal Quantifiers” in very light gray at 29.07%, “Limiter” in light gray at 27.91%, “Negation” in medium gray at 27.91%, and “Existential Quantifiers” in darker gray at 15.12%; the slices appear to be arranged roughly from larger to smaller with the smallest segment placed near the top-left. The Approximate Number Generation chart has three slices with internal labels: “Approximate Quantities” in very light gray at 45.03%, “Comparative Relationships” in medium gray at 36.26%, and “Absolute Absence” in darker gray at 18.71%, visually ordered from largest to smallest. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart has two nearly equal halves with internal labels: “Disjunctive” in very light gray at 49.51% and “Conjunctive” in light gray at 50.49%. None of the charts include a separate legend, and no slices are exploded or otherwise visually emphasized beyond differing gray tones and embedded percentage text.
